name: Barbados
tagline: Refined Caribbean Island Life with British Heritage
description: Barbados is the most polished island in the Caribbean, blending pristine beaches with British colonial heritage, excellent infrastructure, and a welcoming Welcome Stamp visa for remote workers and retirees. The cost of living is significantly higher than most Caribbean islands due to heavy import duties, but the quality of life, safety, and English-speaking culture make it a premium destination. Rum, cricket, and turquoise waters define the Bajan lifestyle.

quickFacts.visa: Welcome Stamp visa (12 months, renewable); standard tourist visa 6 months
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of the safest Caribbean islands
quickFacts.climate: Tropical maritime with consistent trade winds
quickFacts.currency: BBD (Barbados Dollar, pegged to USD at 2:1)

housing.description: Basic long-term 1BR in the south-coast strip (Worthing, Hastings, Rockley), dated but near the beach

dining.description: Local fish cutters, rum-shop plates, and the Friday Oistins fish fry a few times a week; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: Basic local private plan (Sagicor) covering Bayview Hospital and Sandy Crest, with Queen Elizabeth Hospital for emergencies. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees should budget more

transportation.description: Government minibuses and ZR vans at a flat fare, plus the occasional taxi; no car

entertainment.description: Free beaches, cricket, east-coast hikes, and a basic gym

1M.lifestyle: A dated but beach-close 1BR in the south-coast strip of Worthing, Hastings, or Rockley is the realistic entry point, because Barbados's import-driven prices put a hard floor under even a frugal budget. Groceries land near double mainland-US prices, electricity is among the most expensive in the region, and basic private health cover costs more than in Latin America. Getting around means the flat-fare minibuses and ZR vans, and most nights are cooked at home with a fish cutter or the Friday Oistins fish fry as the treat. The beach and the Bajan warmth are free, but there is little slack.

housing.description: Nicer south-coast 1BR or small condo with pool access in Dover, Rockley, or Christ Church

dining.description: Out a few times a week at mid-range spots, with the occasional cliffside dinner at Champers

healthcare.description: Fuller local and regional private cover

transportation.description: A cheap older car with insurance, or heavy taxi use

entertainment.description: Catamaran and snorkel trips, a gym, and some golf

2M.lifestyle: A nicer south-coast 1BR or small condo with pool access in Dover, Rockley, or Christ Church buys real comfort on the developed south of the island. Dining out a few nights a week, with the occasional cliffside table at Champers, sits easily in budget alongside fuller private health cover. A cheap older car — carrying Barbados's stiff insurance and fuel costs — replaces the minibus for most trips. Catamaran cruises, snorkeling, a gym, and some golf round out an unhurried Caribbean routine, though import duties keep everyday costs above most island alternatives.

housing.description: Quality south-coast condo or an entry west-coast (St. James) place near the beach

dining.description: Dining out frequently across the south coast, with occasional Platinum Coast nights

healthcare.description: International plan with medical evacuation to Miami or Martinique

transportation.description: An owned car with comprehensive insurance and Barbados's high fuel costs

entertainment.description: Golf, sailing, spa days, and Crop Over festivities

3M.lifestyle: A quality south-coast condo or an entry-level place on the prestigious west coast in St. James opens up beach-close living on the better side of the island. Dining out is frequent across the south with the occasional splurge on the Platinum Coast, and health cover steps up to an international plan with medical evacuation to Miami or Martinique — a meaningful upgrade given the island's limited tertiary care. An owned car handles the 21-mile island easily, if not cheaply. Golf, sailing, spa days, and Crop Over fill the calendar, with real budget margin left despite Barbados's structurally high costs.

housing.description: West-coast Platinum Coast condo or small villa near St. James and Sandy Lane

dining.description: Near-daily quality dining, including the west coast's best — The Cliff, Lone Star, Cin Cin

healthcare.description: Comprehensive international cover with Miami specialist access

transportation.description: A nicer car with premium insurance

entertainment.description: Sandy Lane and Apes Hill golf, occasional yacht charters, VIP Crop Over

domesticHelp.description: Part-time housekeeper two or three days a week

luxuryExtras.description: Business-class travel to the UK and US, island-hopping, and club memberships

5M.lifestyle: A Platinum Coast condo or small villa near St. James and Sandy Lane places daily life on the west coast, home to the Caribbean's priciest real estate. A part-time housekeeper keeps the property, dining is near-daily and includes the island's marquee tables — The Cliff, Lone Star, Cin Cin — and comprehensive international cover carries Miami specialist access. Golf at Sandy Lane or Apes Hill, the occasional yacht charter, and VIP Crop Over define the leisure, with business-class travel to the UK and US built in. Housing still commands a large share here, a reflection of just how expensive the west coast runs.

housing.description: Long-term Platinum Coast luxury villa or beachfront condo in St. James — among the priciest real estate in the Caribbean

dining.description: Routine fine dining at the west coast's best plus private-chef occasions

healthcare.description: International concierge plan, worldwide including the US, with medical evacuation

transportation.description: Luxury vehicles plus charters and a driver when wanted

entertainment.description: Sandy Lane membership, polo, regular yacht charters, and elite events

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper, gardener, and pool maintenance for the property

luxuryExtras.description: First-class global travel, yacht charter, and an unbounded lifestyle budget

10M.lifestyle: A long-term Platinum Coast villa or beachfront condo in St. James — some of the most expensive real estate in the Caribbean — anchors life at the top, staffed by a housekeeper, gardener, and pool crew. Dining is routine fine dining at the west coast's best with private-chef occasions layered in, and an international concierge plan provides worldwide coverage including the US, with evacuation. Luxury vehicles, chartered yachts, Sandy Lane membership, polo, and first-class global travel are all standard. Housing commands the largest share of even this budget, because Barbados's top-end real estate is priced at genuine international-luxury levels — the island's safety, English-speaking culture, and infrastructure are the premium being paid.
